title: Asymptotics of a planar isoperimetric problem with a white-noise volume term
summary: In this work we study the maximal ratio $I$ between the white noise integrated over a set and the perimeter of the set, which can be seen as a random isoperimetric problem, and appears in the random-field Ising model (Ding-Wirth) and min-max optimal matching (Leighton-Shor). In the planar case considered here, such a ratio is scale-invariant and therefore the problem is critical. As such it requires an ultraviolet cutoff, which we impose by restricting to polygonal sets with side-length at least 1 contained in the ball $B_L$.
